test_title: PYST 81: SSC CGL 2024 - General Knowledge (Held On 26 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a key focus area of the ‘Amrit Dharohar’ scheme launched by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi on World Environment Day, 2023?

options.text: Preservation of ancient Indian heritage sites
To promote values of local communities in conserving wetland ecosystem

solution:
The correct answer is __**To promote values of local communities in conserving wetland ecosystem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Amrit Dharohar' scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on World Environment Day, 2023.
 
• The scheme aims to encourage the preservation and restoration of wetlands in India by involving local communities.
 
• It focuses on the sustainable use of wetland resources while ensuring ecological balance and biodiversity conservation.
 
• Local communities are key stakeholders in this initiative, and their traditional knowledge and practices play a crucial role in wetland conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wetlands**

 
 
• Wetlands are areas where water covers the soil, or is present either at or near the surface of the soil all year or for varying periods of time during the year.
 
• They include swamps, marshes, bogs, and similar areas.
 
• Wetlands provide numerous ecosystem services such as water purification, flood control, and habitat for a wide variety of wildlife.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Balance**
 
 
• Ecological balance refers to a state of dynamic equilibrium within a community of organisms in which genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity remain relatively stable.
 
• It is achieved through the interactions among organisms and their environment.
 
• Conservation efforts like the 'Amrit Dharohar' scheme help maintain ecological balance by protecting and restoring natural habitats.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity Conservation**
 
 
• Biodiversity conservation is the practice of protecting and preserving the variety of species in a particular habitat.
 
• It ensures the survival of species and the health of ecosystems.
 
• Efforts to conserve biodiversity include protecting natural habitats, restoring degraded ecosystems, and implementing sustainable resource management practices.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Knowledge**
 
 
• Traditional knowledge refers to the knowledge, innovations, and practices of indigenous and local communities developed from experience gained over the centuries and adapted to the local culture and environment.
 
• This knowledge is passed down through generations and is an integral part of their cultural heritage.
 
• In the context of wetland conservation, traditional knowledge can provide valuable insights into sustainable management practices and the maintenance of ecological balance.
